definition: Once the profit at the bar's best rate reaches offset, a stop distance below that rate of share times the profit, held between min_distance and max_distance, moved only in the trade's favour.
boundaries: Before the offset the level is missing and the unit's own initial stop holds. The rate is the bar's high for a long and its low for a short, as freqtrade's backtest reads it, so a bar that spikes and closes back sets the stop from the spike. It never widens. Which exits and halts a unit may use, and their numbers, are the risk session's call (ledger R-04); this entry says what the rule does, not whether to use it. QML's unit runtime does not yet pass an exit its position, so inside a unit this exit stays silent until it does. One instance serves one position at a time on its side, and the entry price names the position: an entry price other than the one it holds starts a new position with fresh state. Two positions back to back at the very same entry price would share state until the runtime names each position.
recognition: After a set profit the stop follows the price, keeping half the profit.

class_meanings.perp: freqtrade scales a futures trade's profit ratio by its leverage; this ratio is the price's, before leverage.
class_meanings.index_cfd: a gap across the close moves past the level between two bars; the exit reads the next bar.
